IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PAGING - ingress-service (euc2b) high 5xx and connection resets detected. 5xx rate > 10% over 5m. Pager: Sam

Sam: I'm taking this. Observability links please and any quick customer impact notes.

Maria: Envoy clusters in euc2b are logging lots of upstream reset errors, spread across multiple pods. Example:
```
[envoy][2026-03-15T14:02:11Z] upstream reset: reason=connection_failure, host=10.13.22.77:8080, response_code=502
[ingress][2026-03-15T14:02:13Z] request failed: /v1/chat origin=svc-llm pod=ingress-7dq4
```

Raj: Cloud metrics show NLB target health flaps in euc2b starting 14:00. Target registration and immediate failing healthchecks spiking. Also see TCP RST spikes consistent with NIC-level offload problems reported yesterday in provider's status bulletin.

Liz: Support intake: ~10 seats across 6 customers reported intermittent 502/504s from euc2 endpoints. One enterprise reported retries triggered and increased error alerts. I'm drafting customer-facing note.

Sam: Priority actions: 1) Reduce traffic to euc2b by adjusting Route53 weights, 2) Put suspect NLB target-group into draining mode, 3) Apply short-term ingress config to cut long-lived keepalives, 4) Monitor for cross-region reroute amplification. Raj take DNS/target changes, Maria take ingress config, Liz handle comms.

Raj: Changing weights: euc2b 65% -> 15% via Route53 weighted policy. Command:
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z9EXAMPLE --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.example","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"euc2b","Weight":15,"TTL":20,"AliasTarget":{...}}}]}'
```
Route change submitted (change-id R0EJAMPLE). TTL 20s.

IncidentBot: Route53 change acknowledged, propagation expected within 20-60s.

Maria: Applying ingress tweak to disable keepalive session reuse across Envoy to force short-lived connections. Patch to daemonset environment var KEEPALIVE_REUSE=false and roll one canary pod.
```
kubectl set env daemonset/ingress-controller KEEPALIVE_REUSE=false -n ingress
```
Canary shows fewer reset spikes.

Raj: Started deregistering targets from tg-0f9a8b in euc2b. Using deregistration delay 240s, leaving a minimum control-plane set to handle internal traffic. CLI:
```
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:... --targets Id=i-0f1a2b3c
```
Deregistration in progress.

Sam: Check for any flapping causing weighted DNS to bounce clients back and forth. Watch for any observations of euc1a showing traffic spike that then returns to euc2b. We want to avoid oscillation.

Raj: Noted. I'm also lowering Route53 healthcheck sensitivity: increasing failure threshold from 2 -> 4 and healthcheck interval 10s -> 30s as interim to avoid thrash. Will open follow-up ticket to revisit healthcheck strategy.

Liz: Customers updated: initial note sent, telling them we detected NLB/infrastructure target flapping in euc2, mitigation underway, we expect reduced errors within minutes.

Maria: After weight shift and draining, euc2b 5xx rate fell from 11.8% -> 2.5% in ~6 minutes. Global 5xx stabilized at ~1.0%. Connection reset logs have slowed.

Jared: Logs from one host indicate repeated netdriver firmware warnings around 13:58 - vendor tag matches provider KB about keepalive offload. Opening cloud provider escalation. Scheduling a vendor call.

Sam: Good progress. Leave a small capacity in euc2b for internal control traffic but avoid sending user requests there for 30m. Maria, gather packet captures from an affected host and upload to incident S3. Use tag INC-2678912345.

Maria: Running tcpdump for 300s and uploading.
```
sudo timeout 300 tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/euc2b-2678912345.pcap 'tcp and (port 80 or port 443)'; aws s3 cp /tmp/euc2b-2678912345.pcap s3://redwood-incident-archives/2678912345.pcap
```
Upload confirmed.

Raj: Provider acknowledged potential NIC offload regression in euc2b and scheduled an immediate control-plane task to reapply host firmware fix. They estimate 2-6 hours for full remediation; our DNS weight shift should cover user traffic.

Liz: Sending follow-up to affected customers: brief explanation, mitigation steps taken, and that we'll follow up with postmortem.

Sam: I'm going to pause the pager escalation. Handoff to Maria for monitoring and post-incident data collection. Please create a postmortem with timeline and assign action owners: Raj (healthcheck & firmware), Jared (provider firmware review), Maria (runbook update + artifacts), Liz (customer comms).

IncidentBot: Pager paused by Sam. Incident state: MITIGATED. Create follow-up ticket INC-2678912345.

Maria: Drafting post-incident doc. Initial hypothesis: host NIC offload/driver regression in euc2b causing target flapping in NLB -> Envoy upstream resets -> 5xx surge. Immediate fixes: Route53 weight shift, NLB target drain, ingress keepalive tweak. Action items recorded in the doc.

Jared: I'll coordinate firmware review with cloud provider and schedule a follow-up runbook update meeting.

Sam: Final checks: verify 5xx < 2% for 30 continuous minutes, no customer escalations open. If stable, we close. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

OpsBot: Thread archived. Monitoring continues for 2h; auto-reopen if 5xx > 5%.
